title: The discovery of electricity
subtitle: From Franklin to Tesla
subject: sciences
description: Electricity was not invented suddenly. It was first observed, then understood, then domesticated. Here are the key steps.

hero.hook: From lightning to the smartphone: two centuries to tame the invisible.

blocks.text: Electricity exists in nature: lightning, electric fish, friction. What changed the world was learning to **produce**, **transportation** and use it.
This story spans more than two centuries, with risky experiments and great rivalries.

In the 18th century, **Benjamin Franklin** showed that lightning is an electrical phenomenon. His kite flying experiment (often told in a fictionalized manner) aims to prove that the sky and the friction machine play with the same force.

blocks.caption: Franklin links lightning and electricity: a dangerous, but foundational idea.

blocks.text: We also invented the **thunder**, a metal rod that offers lightning a safe path to the ground. Electricity leaves mystery to enter engineering.

In the 19th century, **Michael Faraday** showed that a magnet moving near a wire could create an electric current. This is the **induction**. Without this idea, no dynamo, no alternator, no modern power plant.

blocks.caption: Faraday transforms movement and magnetism into current.

blocks.text: Faraday came from a humble background and started as a bookbinder. He learned science by reading what he reliaba.

At the end of the 19th century, two camps clashed. **Thomas Edison** pushes direct current. **Nikola Tesla** (and the Westinghouse company) defend alternating current, which is easier to transport over long distances.

blocks.caption: Alternating current is gaining power in cities.

blocks.text: Alternating current wins for urban networks. The cities light up. Factories are changing pace.
Today, electricity powers hospitals, trains, the internet, refrigerators. The challenge is no longer just to produce it, but to do so cleanly and reliably.
Electricity was understood and then domesticated: Franklin for lightning, Faraday to produce current, Tesla and alternating current to bring it into homes. Our daily lives still depend on it.
